note: Canonical game state-machine tree (one source, three views). done[app] = 0..1, how finished our 1:1 work is on that screen for that app (Qud = reference/how well we detect+drive it; Raves = render/impl fidelity). Edit freely; the cockpit reloads on file change. detect[app] recognises 'we are here' from live signals: game_live (Qud's 48710 bridge pushes a snapshot on connect ONLY when a game is actually running — the true menu-vs-in-game signal; the raw port is open even at the main menu, so it can't tell them apart), port (raw listener open = modded Qud alive), and ocr_any (case-insensitive substrings in an OCR of the window). A node matches when all its conditions hold; the DEEPEST match wins. Conditions needing OCR only match on an OCR-enabled poll, so cheap polls fall back to the coarsest ancestor.

costs._note: What a step costs us -- not seconds, but how much we want to AVOID it. Overlays plan.DEFAULT_COSTS. Bridge commands are near-free and never miss; click_text is dear because OCR is the one class that goes flaky, and a missed match does not fail cleanly, it clicks the wrong thing; launch is slow; restart always works and is therefore the last thing the planner should reach for.

preflight.note: GHOST MODAL self-heal. UIManager.popupMessages is a free pool and a RELEASED copy still looks live, so the mod can report scene=PopupMessage with nothing on screen -- and Qud swallows every key while it thinks a modal is up. That is what made the equipment key look broken for a whole session. It is a CONDITION sitting on top of a state, not a state: modelling it as a node would double the graph and as an edge it would need a self-loop, which a shortest-path search cannot use. So it runs before planning, and the plan is made against what is actually there. This one declaration replaced sixteen copy-pasted dismiss steps across the status-tab recipes.

transitions.note: COLD START. No `unless_running` guard any more: the planner only picks this edge from `off`, which is exactly what that flag was hand-checking on every run.

THE UNIVERSAL ESCAPE HATCH, and the reason there is always a route. Every state that has no modelled exit -- the tombstone (injected Esc is ignored there), an unmodelled modern screen, or `unknown` after a cheap poll -- can still reach the title by restarting. Cost 120 keeps it last: the planner takes any chain of first-party moves over it, and picking it AT ALL is the signal that a real exit edge is missing.

LEAVE A LIVE GAME, first-party throughout: CmdQuit goes through Qud's own command path and the confirms are answered BY BUTTON via the mod, so nothing here depends on synthesized keys -- which Qud's modern UI ignores outright. Yes to 'are you sure you want to quit', then NO to 'do you want to save first': Yes would overwrite the fixture save with whatever state the harness drove the character into, destroying the reference every parity capture is measured against.

MEASURED FLAKY, priced accordingly. uiback reaches the active window's own OnCancel/Exit, which covers the other modern menus -- but ModernHighScores did NOT budge when this was measured directly (2026-08-06, both from the daemon and from a raw socket, so it is the screen and not the transport). transitions.note: Kept as conditional `dismiss` steps rather than flattened to plain keys: each one verifies that the thing it pressed actually moved, and a blind Space on a screen with no confirm up does something else entirely.

THE EDGE THAT FIXES TAB-TO-TAB. Raves reaches each tab by pressing its key from in_game, so switching tabs means leaving the current one first. In the recipe model each tab recipe carried its own eight-scene dismiss AND a chain step to in_game whose own recipe routed through `title` -- which from a status screen dismissed it, landed in the game and failed its own assert. Tab-to-tab alternated pass/fail. Here it is one edge the planner inserts when, and only when, it is needed.
